verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: normalizeLocale calls parts[1].toUpperCase() without checking that a separator exists, so input with no '-' or '_' leaves parts[1] undefined and throws TypeError. WHY: checkProfileFields invokes normalizeLocale for any string locale, so PATCH /profile with locale:'en' (or '') crashes with an unhandled TypeError/500 instead of returning a 400 validation error. HOW: guard the missing segment, e.g. default the region to '' or throw an HttpError(400) when parts.length < 2.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: normalizeLocale splits on '-' after replacing the first '_'; for input without a separator (e.g. 'en' or '') parts[1] is undefined, so parts[1].toUpperCase() throws a TypeError. checkProfileFields (line 39-42) calls normalizeLocale for any string locale before validating against SUPPORTED_LOCALES, and updateProfile passes req.body through it, so PATCH /profile with locale:'en' crashes with an unhandled error rather than a 400. The root cause and failure path are correct and not covered by any previous review decision.

WHY: usersRepo.update writes every key of the patch to the users row (see src/users/users.repo.ts:20), so a caller can send {plan:'pro'}, {emailVerified:true}, {email:'attacker@evil'} or {organizationId:'<another tenant>'} and escalate billing/privileges, change their own email for account takeover, or move into another tenant's organization. HOW: replace the blacklist with a whitelist of self-editable fields (displayName, bio, avatarUrl, locale) and build the patch from only those keys.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Verified: sanitizeProfileUpdate (src/users/profile.controller.ts:55-61) only deletes ['id','role','passwordHash'], and updateProfile passes the resulting patch straight to usersRepo.update (line 66). users.repo.ts:20 explicitly writes every key of the patch to the users row, and the User type (lines 3-15) includes sensitive columns not blacklisted: organizationId, email, emailVerified, and plan. No upstream schema/middleware restricting the body was found (grep for updateProfile/sanitizeProfileUpdate/route registration returned only the controller). So a caller can send {plan:'pro'}, {emailVerified:true}, {email:'attacker@evil'} or {organizationId:'<other tenant>'} and have them persisted — the described privilege/billing escalation, account takeover, and cross-tenant move are reachable. The finding's root cause and failure path are accurate; it does not duplicate any PreviousReviewDecisions entry (all concern src/reports/*).

verificationEvidence.claim: WHAT: checkProfileFields guards every rule with `typeof … === 'string'`, so a non-string value for displayName/bio/locale/avatarUrl skips validation entirely, and usersRepo.update (documented as writing every key of the patch) persists it into the users row. WHY: a client can send e.g. `displayName` as an array/object/number, bypassing the 64-char limit and writing a value that violates the `User.displayName: string` contract, breaking downstream consumers. HOW: reject non-string values explicitly, e.g. `if ('displayName' in patch && typeof patch.displayName !== 'string') throw new HttpError(400, 'displayName must be a string');` and the same for bio/locale/avatarUrl before the length/normalization checks.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed. checkProfileFields guards each rule with `typeof … === 'string'`, so a non-string displayName/bio/locale/avatarUrl (array/object/number) bypasses all length, URL and locale checks. sanitizeProfileUpdate only strips PROTECTED_FIELDS (id/role/passwordHash), leaving such values in the patch, and usersRepo.update is documented and implemented to write every key of the patch into the users row. No zod/body-validation schema exists in src/users, so nothing upstream rejects non-string values before persistence, producing a User row that violates the string contract. The described failure path is real and reachable.
